observed_behavior: Real Python stdio MCP handshake/tools-list reports cwd, reserved directories and one-pass argument/environment substitution. Unknown placeholders remain opaque. Relative package executable launches from its canonical package location.

Canonical discovery source plus stable plugin identity determines a host config/plugin-data hash namespace; package replacement preserves existing user data, while distinct plugins remain isolated. Data directory leaf aliases are rejected, including aliases within the shared host data root.

Existing path prefixes are canonicalized. Missing cwd is admitted but never created under the package; process launch fails until it exists. Cwd and package executable paths are checked again immediately before actual spawn.

Local environment references are resolved without logging values. Explicit reserved variables are rejected, remote execution and unavailable references fail clearly. Legacy unconfigured cwd and literal arguments retain existing host behavior.

The host-generated shiju/plugin-process-context ACP metadata carries root/data/cwd without global mutable maps; plugin ACP-array declarations cannot inject that reserved context. Existing non-plugin server behavior is unchanged.
intentional_safety_differences: Legacy host cwd must remain in the package; reserved PLUGIN_ROOT/PLUGIN_DATA cannot be overridden by object-style plugin env or environment references. This is a fail-closed restriction beyond legacy snapshot behavior.
Earlier portable path policy still rejects lexical parent components. No security/path policy is relaxed.
deferred_capabilities: No remote environment execution or PathUri-to-host conversion. Such declarations fail explicitly.
Only the VibeWindow MCP launch path consumes the host metadata. External ACP executors are not claimed to honor that extension.
HTTP credential/header application, lifecycle settings and public authorization are owned by later tasks.
Cross-platform evidence remains task 64; this task ran on macOS only.
